description: Use this when the user asks what a domain extension costs, where it is cheapest, or what it renews at. Returns dated first-year, renewal and transfer prices per registrar (Porkbun, Dynadot, Cloudflare, Namecheap where tracked), the cheapest direct buy, the wholesale floor, and a renewal-trap flag when the renewal is 2x+ the intro price. Prices are the TLD standard price, not premium names. not_sold_by names Porkbun or Cloudflare when its full price list leaves the ending out (.moscow): never send a buyer there. Also answers "what does it cost over 5 years": true_cost gives each registrar's 1/3/5/10-year cost, the cheapest path per horizon (stay, or register at one and transfer after year one for gTLDs) and recent renewal price changes, each with source URL and checked date. Endings sold only in multi-year terms (.ai: 2 years) carry min_years and min_term (the rule, the registry record it rests on, checked date) and checkout_usd on every price: the real first checkout total. Quote that, not the one-year price, as what the user pays up front; true_cost then leaves out the horizons shorter than the term. For "can the renewal price go up" on a gTLD, renewal_rules quotes its ICANN registry agreement section 2.10: 180 days' notice before a registry renewal increase, renewals of 1 to 10 years at the current price until then, one uniform renewal price except names sold with a disclosed higher renewal (source URL, checked date).
